subject: Clarification on staged buyout, capped liquidated damages, and termination paths
messages:
From: Julia Yang <julia.yang@stellar-retail.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: purchasing@stellar-retail.com, legal@stellar-retail.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on staged buyout, capped LDs, and termination paths

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal asked me to follow up with a few concrete asks so we can finalize the commercial terms for the dedicated instance. Key points from our side: 

- For regulated stores we need an enforceable remediation path beyond credits when availability/latency repeatedly breaks SLAs — specifically a staged buyout (fee-at-risk) tied to repeated P1/P2 incidents.
- We also need a cap on liquidated damages but expect an explicit cash reserve or escrow to cover near-term exposure while we onboard.
- Termination rights: after N repeat P1s within M days, customer may terminate for convenience and receive a portion of prepaid fees back.

I attached our RFP redlines (SaaS_RFP_Redlines_v2.pdf) with suggested thresholds and examples. Can your legal/sales propose an acceptable structure? We prefer a short written addendum rather than protracted edits to the master SOW.

Available to discuss Thu/Fri this week.

— Julia
Julia Yang | Director, Strategic Sourcing
Stellar Retail
[Attachment: SaaS_RFP_Redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on staged buyout, capped LDs, and termination paths

Julia —

Appreciate the detail and the attached redlines. Quick summary from our side and a couple of immediate clarifying questions so we come prepared to a call: 

1) Redwood position (high level): our standard hosted/dedicated commercial model assumes SLA service credits as primary remedy; termination and cash buyouts are handled for enterprise customers with reserved capacity on a case-by-case basis.

2) For regulated workloads (health/finance/retail with PII), we have historically agreed to escrowed funds or a limited buyout tranche tied to committed spend. We’d need committed capacity numbers and a forecast to size an escrow.

3) Can you confirm the thresholds you’re envisioning (example in your doc references 3 P1s in 60 days -> termination). Are you flexible on cure periods and on whether the buyout is staged (e.g., 25%/50%/100% of monthly committed spend)?

4) Who from Stellar legal should we loop in directly for working redlines? We’ll circulate an initial SLA addendum draft to reduce back-and-forth.

I copied Ben (sales lead) and Vanessa (enterprise legal ops) to help with the addendum and sizing.

If Thu/Fri works, propose Thu 11:00–11:30 PT. If not, send times and we’ll confirm.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick reply. A few specifics from our procurement/legal team: 

- Thresholds we expect to see in language: 3 P1s (full-service outage or >500ms median latency impact on committed traffic) within a 90-day rolling window triggers a buyout right.
- Buyout economics: first trigger = 25% of remaining committed fees, second trigger = 50%, third trigger = full remaining commitment minus any unused prepaid credits.
- We want the buyout funds held in escrow or a certified letter of credit for the initial 6 months.
- Liquidated damages should be capped (we are OK with a cap equal to three months’ committed spend), but the buyout mechanism remains separate (i.e., LD cap does not erase termination/buyout rights).

Legal is sensitive to indefinite cure windows. We’d accept a 7–14 day cure period depending on severity. Please share a Redwood addendum draft that implements these mechanics and any proposed mitigations (grace windows, maintenance blackout windows, scheduled maintenance notice obligations).

Regards,
Purchasing Team
Stellar Retail
[Attachment: Procurement_SLA_Expectations.pdf (pdf)]

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Yang <julia.yang@stellar-retail.com>, purchasing@stellar-retail.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on staged buyout, capped LDs, and termination paths

Hi Julia / Stellar team —

Thanks for the clear thresholds. Hannah looped me in to propose an initial, commercially realistic counterproposal so your legal team and ours have something concrete to react to. High-level offer: 

- Applicability: Dedicated-reserved customers only (to be clear: not standard pay-as-you-go hosted).
- Triggers: 3 P1s in any 90-day rolling window, where P1 is an availability outage affecting >= 20% of committed traffic for >5 minutes OR median tail latency above agreed threshold for >30 minutes.
- Cure: Each incident includes an automatic 72-hour diagnostic/cure window plus a one-time 14-day operational correction window after incident closure where mitigation work must be scheduled.
- Staged buyout schedule: 1st trigger = 20% of remaining committed monthly fees; 2nd trigger = 45%; 3rd trigger = 100% (we will pay out the remainder of prepayments less documented credits).
- Escrow/credit: Redwood is willing to work with a short-term escrow (6 months) or a letter of credit; escrow admin fees to be shared 50/50.
- Cap on LDs: agree to cap LDs at three months’ committed spend but LDs and buyout are treated separately as Stellar requested.

Operational mitigations we propose to reduce false positives: prefix KV caching, dedicated routing to isolate your tenant, scheduled health-check escalation hooks, and a canary rollout window for major runtime upgrades. We’ll add these operational commitments to the SLA addendum.

I’ve uploaded a draft SLA addendum to our shared drive (link below) and attached a redlined doc for quick review (RI_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.docx). If this looks reasonable we’d like to run a short call Thu 11am PT (Hannah suggested) with legal ops on both sides to narrow language.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
